challenge: The sequential Caseflow lifecycle could return only one next task, while independent note-surface work needed concurrency without creating a second workflow authority or allowing exit codes to stand in for verified handoffs.
observedFailure: Knowledge graphs and NodeTrace trajectories existed, but no runtime compiled canonical current-stage work into deterministic, artifact-bound edges or excluded overlapping write scopes before declaring work runnable.
resolution: Added a disposable current-stage execution projection compiled from Caseflow stage-task artifacts, immutable exact-artifact edge bindings, a conflict-free fail-closed runnable frontier, verifier-derived review context, three bounded JSON CLI commands, and public schemas/types. Caseflow and advanceStage retain all lifecycle authority; generated design.md and a new ReviewFinding object were cut.
knownLimitations: Human-attested and NodeProof-verified bindings require a protected embedding-runtime verifier; the file-only CLI refuses them.
Runtime NodeTrace recording belongs to the runner that performs real work and is not fabricated by the pure compiler.
NodeBench, NodeRoom, the full evidence chain, and the paired scheduler experiment remain separate consumer proof.
Persistent native-agent workspace and session identity remains a separate unimplemented authority and continuity contract.
ActiveGraph remains an offline, non-authoritative canary.
Canonical promotion requires a separately verified human approval.
